model: Kimi K3.1 Pro, int8 container written by c/tools/k3_repack.py --bits 8 (94 shards, 1505.7 GB)
command: MODEL=<container on nvme0> RUNS=3 NGEN=64 DRIVES='<block devices of nvme0, nvme1, nvme2, nvme3>' ./bench.sh OUT base-off@<v2.2.0>/c/kimi_k3 pr-off@<this commit>/c/kimi_k3 'pr-mirror@<this commit>/c/kimi_k3@COLI_MODEL_MIRROR=<copy on nvme2>;<copy on nvme3>' (bench.sh in this directory). Each run is a fresh process: env <common.env> kimi_k3 <container> <prompt.txt> --chat --ngen 64, 91 prompt tokens, greedy. Page cache dropped before each run, arms rotated per round, 3 rounds, no warm-up.

hardware.cpu: Intel Core Ultra 7 270K Plus, 24 cores (8 P + 16 E), no SMT
hardware.storage: 4x Samsung 990 PRO 4 TB, each PCIe 4.0 x4. nvme0 (primary) and nvme1 on CPU root ports, nvme2 and nvme3 (the two copies) on Z890 chipset root ports, which share one uplink to the CPU. nvme1 was idle in this run. No drive throttled: the thermal management counters of nvme smart-log did not change, the hottest drive peaked at 66 C.
hardware.os: Ubuntu 24.04.5, kernel 6.8.0-149-generic, gcc 13.3.0, make kimi_k3 ARCH=native

hypothesis: Reading the routed experts of each batch from byte-identical copies on two more drives (round-robin by weight) raises kimi_k3's expert read rate, and so its decode rate, above what the one drive that holds a layer's shard delivers.
